input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 sets a three-year term and Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/service-level/legal/IP failures), with numbering skipping from 9.3 to 9.5 and no convenience right anywhere. Under T4C's detection guidance, the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation. Section 2.1 compounds this by stripping Customer of "termination rights" under a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment, which would nullify any convenience right and operate as a penalty. We therefore insert a numbered Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination fee, confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a term, and make the Section 2.1 commitment subject to Section 9 by deleting only "or termination" and adding a narrow proviso. Vendor is given no convenience right elsewhere in the document, so no deletion is required on that side.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall owe no early-termination fee or other penalty. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

ops.newText: without reduction rights, subject to Customer's termination rights under Section 9.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a new Section 9.4 giving Customer the right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no penalty, and confirming Vendor has no reciprocal walk-away right during a term, as our playbook requires for any term longer than 12 months. We have also made the take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 subject to that right so it does not operate as an early-termination penalty; we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Insert numbered Section 9.4 Customer termination for convenience (30 days, pro-rata refund) and make Section 2.1 take-or-pay subject to Section 9.
